translations.title: Shipping Supplements And Vitamins To Mexico: The Hard Truth
translations.excerpt: Supplements do not need product registration in Mexico, which is why so many sellers assume they are unregulated. They still need an import permit, and health claims will get them seized.
translations.content:
Supplements do not require a product registration in Mexico, but they do require a prior sanitary import permit obtained through the VUTCE (the foreign trade single window, successor to VUTCE) window, an importing business registered by notice of operation, a Spanish label carrying two mandatory phrases, and ingredients within Mexico's maximum daily doses. Any therapeutic or health claim reclassifies the product as a medicine and stops the shipment.

  • Supplements are not on the list of products requiring registro sanitario under the General Health Law, Article 376 (LGS).
  • They do require a prior sanitary import permit, filed through the VUTCE single window and attached to the pedimento (Secretaría de Salud import regulation).
  • The importing business must file an Aviso de Funcionamiento at least 30 days before starting activity (LGS Art. 200 Bis).
  • NOM-051 does not apply to supplements; the binding labelling rules are in the health products regulation, Appendix XVII (COFEPRIS).
  • In February 2026 COFEPRIS issued an alert against a US supplement brand, citing English labelling, health claims and a missing import permit.

Can I sell US supplements in Mexico?

Yes, but not the way most sellers assume. There is no product registration, which is why people think supplements are lightly regulated. What there is instead is a prior import permit, a registered Mexican importer and strict labelling rules, and skipping any of them stops the goods.

The confusion around supplements in Mexico comes from one true fact that gets misread. It is true that supplements do not require a registro sanitario, the product registration that medicines and medical devices need, because Article 376 of the General Health Law lists what needs registration and supplements are not on it. COFEPRIS says the same thing plainly: what supplement makers file is a notice of operation, which does not constitute any kind of authorisation or registration. Many sellers stop reading there and conclude that supplements are effectively unregulated. That conclusion is wrong and expensive. Registration of the product and permission to import the product are two different things, and supplements need the second one. They sit inside the annex of goods whose import is regulated by the health ministry, which means a prior sanitary import permit is mandatory, obtained through the VUTCE single window and attached to the pedimento as an electronic document. In practice a shipment without that permit does not clear. There is a second requirement people miss: the importing business, not the product, must file an Aviso de Funcionamiento with the health authority at least 30 days before it starts operating, and that filing has to name the party responsible. As of August 2025 the permit process was simplified into a single procedure with a four day resolution time instead of five, and the old requirement to submit an original origin label was dropped. So the honest summary is this: you do not register your product, you register your operation and you license each import.

The labelling rules are not the ones you expect

NOM-051, the food labelling standard everyone cites, does not apply to supplements. The binding rules sit in Appendix XVII of the health products regulation, and they require two specific phrases in capitals and bold, plus a full Spanish label before the product is sold.

This is where most published advice about Mexican supplements is simply wrong. Commercial blogs routinely tell sellers to comply with NOM-051, the front of pack food labelling standard, but COFEPRIS states in its own legal framework page that NOM-051 does not apply to supplements, and the economy ministry's application criterion says the same. What actually binds is Appendix XVII of the health products regulation, and it is specific. The label must carry the generic and specific product name, a full ingredient list in order of quantity, and where the product contains plants, both the common name and the botanical name at genus and species level. It must state any component that could pose a health risk, a nutritional declaration, the name and address of the manufacturer or importer, packer and distributor, instructions for storage, preparation and consumption, the lot number and the expiry date. Then there are two phrases that must appear together, in capital letters, in bold and in a contrasting colour, at the same point size as the rest of the information panel, with a clear space around them of at least one letter height. The first is that this product is not a medicine. The second is that consumption of this product is the responsibility of whoever recommends it and whoever uses it. Minimum letter height is set by the area of the information panel, starting at half a millimetre for very small panels and rising to three millimetres for panels above 161 square centimetres. And the label must be in Spanish before the product is offered for sale, not after it arrives. For imported goods packaged at origin, the regulation is explicit that the Spanish information has to be there prior to commercialisation, which is why labelling at origin is almost always cheaper than relabelling in Mexico.

Health claims and banned ingredients are what actually gets you seized

Mexico bans therapeutic claims outright, and a claim can reclassify your supplement as a medicine. Specific substances are prohibited, and vitamins and minerals have hard maximum daily doses. A February 2026 COFEPRIS alert against a US brand hit all of these at once.

The rules that most often stop a shipment are not paperwork rules, they are content rules. On ingredients, the regulation names substances that supplements must not contain: procaine, ephedrine, yohimbine, germanium, animal or human hormones, plants that are not permitted for infusions or teas, and any recognised pharmacological substance or anything representing a health risk. If your product contains a little known substance that could pose a risk, both its processing and its import depend on proving harmlessness scientifically to COFEPRIS first. Vitamins and minerals carry hard maximum daily doses, and exceeding them can push a product out of the supplement category altogether. Vitamin A is capped at 1000 micrograms, vitamin C at 300 milligrams, vitamin D at 10 micrograms, vitamin E at 200 milligrams, iron at 20 milligrams, zinc at 20 milligrams and calcium at 1200 milligrams, among others. On claims, the position is stricter than most US sellers expect. The regulation prohibits labelling or advertising that confuses, exaggerates or misleads, and specifically prohibits showing any preventive, rehabilitative or therapeutic indication. Labels cannot reference a disease, symptom, syndrome, anatomical feature or physiological process, and cannot claim the product replaces a meal or covers nutritional needs on its own. Brand names themselves cannot contain such references. If the authority attributes a therapeutic property to your product, it is legally treated as a medicine, which means it cannot be sold without meeting medicine rules. This is not theoretical. In February 2026 COFEPRIS issued a health alert against a US supplement brand sold through e-commerce platforms and apps, citing therapeutic claims such as restoring mental clarity and supporting healthy immune function, an English language label, prohibited plant ingredients, and the absence of both product registration and an import permit. The alert stated the products must not be distributed by any route, expressly including national and international courier and parcel services. One more change worth noting: a reform published in January 2026 added supplements explicitly to the article of the General Health Law covering sanitary control of processing, import and export, which puts the category on firmer statutory ground rather than changing the day to day rules. Frequently asked questions

Do supplements need registration to be sold in Mexico?

No product registration is required, because supplements are not on the list in Article 376 of the General Health Law. But this is where most sellers go wrong: registration and import permission are different things. Supplements do require a prior sanitary import permit for each import, filed through VUTCE and attached to the customs declaration.

Does NOM-051 apply to supplements in Mexico?

No. COFEPRIS states in its own legal framework that NOM-051 does not apply to supplements, and the economy ministry's application criterion agrees. Much commercial advice online says otherwise and is wrong. The binding labelling rules are in Appendix XVII of the health products regulation, which sets different and more specific requirements.

What must a Mexican supplement label say?

The product name, full ingredient list in order of quantity with botanical names for plants, risk components, nutritional declaration, importer name and address, storage and use instructions, lot number and expiry date. Two phrases are mandatory in capitals and bold: that the product is not a medicine, and that consumption is the responsibility of whoever recommends and uses it.

Can I make health claims on supplements in Mexico?

No. The regulation prohibits any preventive, rehabilitative or therapeutic indication, and bans references to diseases, symptoms, syndromes or physiological processes on the label or in the brand name. If the authority attributes a therapeutic property to your product it is legally treated as a medicine and cannot be sold as a supplement.

Which ingredients are banned in Mexican supplements?

The regulation names procaine, ephedrine, yohimbine, germanium, animal or human hormones, plants not permitted for teas and infusions, and any recognised pharmacological substance or health risk. Vitamins and minerals also carry maximum daily doses, for example 1000 micrograms of vitamin A and 300 milligrams of vitamin C, and exceeding them can push the product out of the supplement category.

translations.title: Shein-Temu Vergisi: Kurye Paketlerine Gelen Düzenleme Ve Fırsat
translations.excerpt: Meksika'nın Shein-Temu vergisi diye anılan düzenlemesi Çin'i hedefliyor ama Türkiye'yi de aynı kefeye koyuyor. Rakamlar ve Türk satıcı için gerçek sonuç.
translations.content:
Meksika'da anlaşması olmayan ülkelerden gelen kurye paketleri ilk dolardan itibaren yüzde 33,5 birleşik oran ödüyor. T-MEC ülkelerinden gelenler çok daha hafif: 50 dolara kadar muaf, 50-117 dolar arası yüzde 17, üzeri yüzde 19. Türkiye anlaşmasız ülke olduğu için Türk malı da yüzde 33,5 bandındadır, yani bu düzenleme Türk satıcı için doğrudan bir fırsat değildir.

  • Anlaşmasız menşe (Çin, Türkiye dahil) kurye paketleri ilk dolardan yüzde 33,5 birleşik oran öder (RGCE 2026, Regla 3.7.35).
  • T-MEC menşeli paketler: 50 dolara kadar muaf, 50-117 dolar yüzde 17, 117 doların üzeri yüzde 19 (RGCE 2026).
  • Bu oranlar birleşik orandır (tasa global): IVA, gümrük vergisi ve işlem harcı içine gömülüdür, ayrıca yüzde 16 IVA eklenmez (Ley Aduanera md. 88 bis).
  • Oran 15 Ağustos 2025'te yüzde 19'dan yüzde 33,5'e çıktı; karar DOF'ta 28 Temmuz 2025'te yayımlandı (DOF).
  • Basitleştirilmiş kurye rejiminin üst sınırı alıcı başına 2.500 dolardır; üzeri normal pedimento ve gümrük müşaviri gerektirir (RGCE 2026).

Shein-Temu vergisi Türk satıcıya fırsat mı?

Doğrudan hayır. Düzenleme Çin merkezli platformları hedefliyor ama menşeye göre çalışıyor, ülkeye göre değil. Türkiye'nin Meksika ile yürürlükte serbest ticaret anlaşması olmadığı için Türk malı da aynı yüzde 33,5 bandına giriyor.

Bu soruya dürüst cevap vermek gerekiyor, çünkü piyasada aksi yönde çok yorum dolaşıyor. Meksika'nın Shein-Temu vergisi diye anılan düzenlemesi gerçekte bir platform vergisi değil, menşe temelli bir kurye tarifesidir. Kural şöyle işliyor: T-MEC ülkelerinden, yani ABD ve Kanada'dan gelen kurye sevkiyatları kademeli ve hafif bir rejime tabi. 50 dolara kadar olan sevkiyatta gümrük vergisi de katma değer vergisi de alınmıyor, sadece işlem harcı ödeniyor. 50 ile 117 dolar arasında yüzde 17, 117 doların üzerinde yüzde 19 birleşik oran uygulanıyor. Anlaşması olmayan her menşe ise ilk dolardan itibaren yüzde 33,5 ödüyor ve hiçbir muafiyet eşiği yok. Buradaki kritik nokta Türkiye'nin bu tabloda nerede durduğu. Türkiye'nin Meksika ile yürürlükte bir serbest ticaret anlaşması bulunmuyor; Ekonomi Bakanlığı'nın anlaşmalı ülkeler listesinde Türkiye yer almıyor, mevcut olan ticari işbirliği anlaşması tercihli tarife tanımıyor. Dolayısıyla Türkiye menşeli bir mal, Çin menşeli bir malla tam olarak aynı bantta, yüzde 33,5'te. Yani Çin'in maliyeti arttı diye Türk satıcının rekabet avantajı doğmuyor; ikisinin de maliyeti aynı oranda arttı. Bu düzenlemeyi fırsat diye sunan içeriklere temkinli yaklaş, çünkü menşe kuralını atlıyorlar.

Rakamlar tam olarak ne ve ne zaman değişti?

Anlaşmasız menşe oranı 15 Ağustos 2025'te yüzde 19'dan yüzde 33,5'e çıktı. Bu oran birleşik orandır, üstüne ayrıca yüzde 16 IVA eklenmez. Ayrıca 1 Ocak 2026'da yürürlüğe giren ayrı bir tarife kararnamesi var ve ikisi sık karıştırılıyor.

İki ayrı düzenleme var ve bunları karıştırmak en sık yapılan hata. Birincisi kurye rejimindeki oran değişikliği. Karar 28 Temmuz 2025'te Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı ve 15 Ağustos 2025'te yürürlüğe girdi; anlaşmasız menşe için oran yüzde 19'dan yüzde 33,5'e çıktı. Yani bugün yüzde 19 oranı yalnızca T-MEC menşeli ve değeri 117 doların üzerindeki sevkiyatlara uygulanıyor. Burada çok önemli bir teknik ayrıntı var: bu oranlar birleşik orandır. Gümrük Kanunu'nun ilgili maddesine göre bu faktör, katma değer vergisi oranı, gümrük işlem harcı ve tarife cetvelindeki en yüksek oran birlikte hesaplanarak bulunuyor. Yani yüzde 33,5 ödedikten sonra ayrıca yüzde 16 IVA ödemiyorsun; IVA zaten o oranın içinde. Bunu yanlış anlatan kaynaklar maliyeti olduğundan yüksek gösteriyor. İkinci düzenleme ise tarife kararnamesi: 29 Aralık 2025'te yayımlanıp 1 Ocak 2026'da yürürlüğe giren karar, bin dörtyüzden fazla tarife pozisyonunda oranları yüzde 5 ile 50 arasına çıkardı ve tekstil, ayakkabı, kozmetik, oyuncak gibi kalemleri kapsıyor. Ama bu kararname normal pedimento ile yapılan ithalatı etkiliyor, kurye rejimindeki birleşik oranı otomatik olarak değiştirmedi. Yani Shein paketleri Ocak 2026'da yüzde 50'ye çıktı demek yanlış olur. Bir de sınır bölgesi meselesi: kuzey sınırdaki yüzde 8 katma değer vergisi teşviki mal ithalatına uygulanmıyor, sadece bölgedeki satış ve hizmetleri kapsıyor.

Peki Türk satıcı maliyeti nasıl düşürür?

İki gerçek yol var: paket paket göndermek yerine ABD'de konsolide edip tek ithalat yapmak, ya da hacim büyüdüğünde 2.500 dolar sınırını aşıp normal pedimentoya geçmek. Paketi bölerek muafiyet kovalamak ise raporlanan bir davranış.

Fırsat düzenlemede değil, operasyon modelinde. Birinci ve en gerçekçi yol konsolidasyon. Türkiye'den tek tek kurye paketi göndermek yerine malı ABD'deki bir depoda toplayıp Meksika'ya tek sevkiyat olarak göndermek, gümrük işlem maliyetlerini çok daha fazla mala böler. Burada dikkat edilmesi gereken bir hukuki nüans var ve dürüst olmak gerekiyor: kurye kuralının metni anlaşma tarafı bir ülkeden gelen sevkiyatlar ifadesini kullanıyor, yani sevkiyatın çıkış ülkesine atıf yapıyor ve menşe şahadetnamesi şart koşmuyor. Karşılaştırma olarak başka bir kural tercihli oran için menşe belgesini açıkça istiyor, kurye kuralında böyle bir şart yok. Bunun pratikte nasıl uygulandığına dair yayımlanmış resmî bir görüş bulamadık, o yüzden bunu kesin bir hüküm gibi alma ve mutlaka gümrük müşavirinle teyit et. İkinci yol hacim büyüdüğünde rejim değiştirmek. Basitleştirilmiş kurye rejiminin üst sınırı alıcı başına 2.500 dolar; üzerine çıktığında normal pedimento, gümrük müşaviri ve ithalatçı kaydı gerekiyor. Bu daha çok evrak demek ama tarife artık malın kendi pozisyonuna göre hesaplanıyor, tek bir yüksek birleşik orana değil, ve menşe belgesi olan mallarda avantaj doğabiliyor. Kaçınman gereken yol ise net: siparişi 49 dolarlık parçalara bölerek muafiyet kovalamak. Kural bunu öngörmüş; kurye şirketi aynı alıcı veya aynı teslimat adresi için ayda üçten fazla muafiyet işlemi yaparsa idareye bildirim yapmak zorunda. Ayrıca değeri sıfır gösterilen, değeri belirtilmeyen veya içeriği çeşitli ürünler, hediye gibi genel ifadelerle tanımlanan gönderiler basitleştirilmiş rejime hiç giremiyor. BringGo Ship, Laredo ve Monterrey depoları ve lisanslı gümrük müşaviriyle tam da bu konsolidasyon modelini işletiyor.

Tanımlar

  • Birleşik oran (tasa global): Birleşik oran, gümrük vergisi, katma değer vergisi ve işlem harcını tek bir yüzdede toplayan orandır, üstüne ayrıca IVA eklenmez.
  • Basitleştirilmiş kurye rejimi: Basitleştirilmiş kurye rejimi, alıcı başına 2.500 dolara kadar sevkiyatların pedimento yerine tek oranla geçtiği hızlı gümrük yoludur.
  • Anlaşmasız menşe: Anlaşmasız menşe, Meksika ile yürürlükte serbest ticaret anlaşması bulunmayan ülkeden gelen maldır ve Türkiye bu gruptadır.

Sık sorulan sorular

Shein-Temu vergisi Türk satıcıya fırsat mı?

Doğrudan hayır. Düzenleme platformu değil menşeyi hedefliyor. Türkiye'nin Meksika ile yürürlükte serbest ticaret anlaşması olmadığı için Türk malı da Çin malıyla aynı yüzde 33,5 bandına giriyor. Yani Çin'in maliyeti arttığında Türk satıcının otomatik bir avantajı doğmuyor, ikisinin maliyeti de aynı oranda arttı.

Meksika'da kurye paketlerine hangi oran uygulanıyor?

Anlaşmasız menşede ilk dolardan itibaren yüzde 33,5 birleşik oran. T-MEC menşeli sevkiyatlarda ise 50 dolara kadar muafiyet, 50-117 dolar arası yüzde 17 ve 117 doların üzerinde yüzde 19 uygulanıyor. Basitleştirilmiş rejimin üst sınırı alıcı başına 2.500 dolar, üzeri normal pedimento gerektiriyor.

Yüzde 33,5'in üstüne ayrıca IVA ödeniyor mu?

Hayır. Bu bir birleşik orandır ve gümrük vergisi, katma değer vergisi ile işlem harcı zaten içine gömülüdür. Kanun metni bu faktörün katma değer vergisi oranı, işlem harcı ve tarife cetvelindeki en yüksek oran birlikte hesaplanarak bulunduğunu söylüyor. Ayrıca yüzde 16 IVA ekleyen hesaplar maliyeti olduğundan yüksek gösterir.

Oran ne zaman ve ne kadar arttı?

Anlaşmasız menşe oranı 15 Ağustos 2025'te yüzde 19'dan yüzde 33,5'e çıktı; karar 28 Temmuz 2025'te Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Bugün yüzde 19 yalnızca T-MEC menşeli ve 117 doların üzerindeki sevkiyatlar için geçerli. Ocak 2026'daki tarife kararnamesi ayrı bir düzenlemedir ve kurye birleşik oranını otomatik değiştirmedi.

Siparişi küçük parçalara bölerek muafiyetten yararlanabilir miyim?

Bu riskli ve kural bunu öngörmüş. Kurye şirketi aynı alıcı veya aynı teslimat adresi için bir takvim ayında üçten fazla muafiyet işlemi yaparsa idareye bildirim yapmak zorunda. Ayrıca vergi kaçırmak amacıyla planlanmış sevkiyat serileri ile değeri sıfır gösterilen veya içeriği genel ifadelerle tanımlanan gönderiler bu rejime hiç giremiyor.

translations.title: Meksika HS Kodu (GTİP) Bulma: Fracción Arancelaria Rehberi
translations.excerpt: Türk GTİP'i 12 hane, Meksika kodu 10 hane, ama ilk 6 hane ikisinde de aynı. Doğru kodu nasıl bulacağını ve 2026'da neyin değiştiğini anlatıyoruz.
translations.content:
Meksika tarife kodu 10 hanedir: ilk 8 hane fracción arancelaria, son 2 hane NICO. İlk 6 hane uluslararası HS kodudur ve Türk GTİP'inizin ilk 6 hanesiyle birebir aynıdır, çünkü iki ülke de HS 2022 uygular. Kodu SNICE ve VUTCE (dış ticaret tek pencere sistemi, VUTCE'in devamı) üzerinden araştırabilirsiniz, ama bağlayıcı cevap için SAT'a başvurmanız gerekir.

  • Meksika kodu 10 hanedir: 8 hane fracción arancelaria artı 2 hane NICO; örnek gösterim 8708.29.99 99 (RGCE 2026).
  • İlk 6 hane uluslararası HS kodudur ve Türk GTİP'in ilk 6 hanesiyle aynıdır; iki ülke de HS 2022 uygular (HS Sözleşmesi md. 3).
  • Yürürlükteki LIGIE 7 Haziran 2022 tarihlidir ve 12 Aralık 2022'de yürürlüğe girmiştir; 2020 tarihli LIGIE ilga edilmiştir (DOF).
  • Bağlayıcı sınıflandırma görüşü için işlemden önce SAT'a başvurulur (Gümrük Kanunu md. 47).
  • 1 Ocak 2026'dan itibaren yanlış veya eksik NICO da açıkça cezalandırılabilir bir alan hâline geldi (RGCE 2026 Anexo 19).

Ürünümün Meksika GTİP kodunu nasıl bulurum?

İlk 6 haneyi zaten biliyorsun: Türk GTİP'inin ilk 6 hanesi aynen geçerli, çünkü iki ülke de HS 2022 uyguluyor. Kalan 4 haneyi, yani fracción arancelaria'nın son 2 hanesi ile NICO'yu, Meksika'nın kendi tarife cetvelinden bulman gerekiyor.

İyi haberle başlayalım: işin yarısı zaten elinde. Meksika kodunun ilk 6 hanesi uluslararası Armonize Sistem kodudur ve Türkiye ile Meksika'nın ikisi de HS 2022 sürümünü uyguladığı için bu 6 hane birebir aynıdır. Bunun hukuki dayanağı var: HS Sözleşmesi, taraf ülkelerin tüm pozisyon ve alt pozisyonları hiçbir ekleme veya değişiklik yapmadan kullanmasını, kendi alt açılımlarını ancak 6 hanenin ötesinde yapmasını şart koşuyor. Yani ürününün Türkiye'deki GTİP'inin ilk 6 hanesini alıp Meksika tarafında aynı yerden devam edebilirsin. Farklılık bundan sonra başlıyor. Türk GTİP'i 12 hanedir: ilk 6 hane HS, 7 ve 8. haneler Avrupa Birliği Kombine Nomanklatür kodu, 9 ve 10. haneler Türkiye'nin kendi farklı vergi uygulamaları için açtığı millî haneler, 11 ve 12. haneler istatistik kodudur. Meksika ise 10 hane kullanır: ilk 8 hane fracción arancelaria, son 2 hane ise NICO'dur. Burada sık yapılan bir hata var: fracción arancelaria 7 ve 8. haneler değil, 8 hanenin tamamıdır. Meksika mevzuatının kendi gösterimi bunu net yapıyor, örneğin 8708.29.99 99 kodunda ilk sekiz hane fracción arancelaria'ya, son iki hane NICO'ya karşılık gelir. Pratikte yapman gereken şu: ilk 6 haneyi Türk GTİP'inden al, sonra Meksika tarife cetvelinde o alt pozisyonun altındaki fracción seçeneklerine bak ve ürününü tarif eden 8 haneli kodu belirle, ardından o fracción'a bağlı NICO listesinden doğru 2 haneyi seç.

Hangi resmî araçları kullanmalısın?

SNICE ve VUTCE'in Clasificador Arancelario'su güncel ve çalışıyor. Ama ikisi de bilgilendirme amaçlıdır, bağlayıcı değildir. SIAVI'yi kullanma, 2022 Şubatından beri güncellenmiyor.

Araç seçimi önemli, çünkü internette dolaşan tavsiyelerin bir kısmı artık ölü sistemleri işaret ediyor. Kullanılabilir iki resmî kaynak var. Birincisi SNICE, yani Dış Ticaret Ulusal Bilgi Servisi. Ekonomi Bakanlığı'na bağlıdır ve LIGIE metnini, NICO kataloğunu, tarife dışı düzenlemeleri ve korelasyon tablolarını yayınlar; güncel fracción listesini tablo hâlinde indirebilirsin. İkincisi VUTCE'in Clasificador Arancelario'su, yani tek pencere sistemindeki fracción arama aracı. İkisi de çalışıyor ve güncel, ama ikisi de bilgilendirme amaçlıdır; verdikleri sonuç idareyi bağlamaz. Kullanmaman gereken iki kaynak var. SIAVI, kendi sayfasındaki nota göre Şubat 2022'den itibaren güncellenmiyor ve verileri Kasım 2021'de duruyor, dolayısıyla 2026'da güncel tarife aracı olarak kullanılamaz. SIICEX ise erişilemez durumda, içeriği SNICE'ye taşınmış; benzer adlı bir site hâlâ yayında ama o gümrük müşavirleri konfederasyonunun özel abonelik hizmetidir, resmî devlet kaynağı değildir. Bir de şu ayrıntıya dikkat: hangi LIGIE'ye baktığın önemli. Yürürlükteki LIGIE 7 Haziran 2022 tarihlidir ve 12 Aralık 2022'de yürürlüğe girmiştir; 1 Temmuz 2020 tarihli LIGIE ilga edilmiştir. Ayrıca tarife oranları sık değişiyor: 29 Aralık 2025 tarihli kararname 1 Ocak 2026'da yürürlüğe girip binden fazla pozisyonda oranları artırdı, 23 Nisan 2026 tarihli bir başka kararname 185 pozisyonda değişiklik yaptı. Yani kodu bulman yetmez, o koda bağlı güncel oranı da işlem anında kontrol etmen gerekir.

Bağlayıcı cevap ve yanlışın bedeli

Kesin cevap için işlemden önce SAT'a başvurabilirsin; başvuru sürerken malı en yüksek aday oranı ödeyerek çekebilirsin. Ticari tanım fiziki malla örtüşüyorsa yanlış kod kaçakçılık değil, evrak hatası sayılır ve cezası sınırlıdır.

Emin olamıyorsan tahmin etme, sor. Meksika Gümrük Kanunu, ithalatçı, ihracatçı ve gümrük müşavirlerinin işlemden önce SAT'a sınıflandırma ve NICO sorusu sormasına izin veriyor; bu, ürünün birden fazla pozisyona girebileceğini düşündüğünde veya kodu hiç bilmediğinde geçerli. Bu mekanizmanın en pratik yanı şu: başvurun sürerken malı gümrükten çekebilirsin, aday kodlar arasından en yüksek oranlı olanı ödeyerek. Ayrıca gümrük denetiminde sınıflandırmaya ilişkin bir aykırılık tespit edilirse, memurlar başvurun sonuçlanana kadar ilgili yaptırım kararlarını çıkarmıyorlar. Bunun yanında gümrükleme öncesi teknik danışma toplantısı talep etme imkânı da var; talep üzerine iki gün içinde tarih veriliyor ve beş gün içinde toplanıyor. Yanlış sınıflandırmanın bedeline gelince, en kritik bilgi şu ve çoğu kaynak bunu yazmıyor: eğer pedimentoda beyan edilen ticari tanım fiziksel olarak sunulan malla örtüşüyorsa, yanlış fracción kaçakçılık kapsamına girmez, pedimentoda hatalı veri beyanı sayılır ve cezası belge başına iki bin altı yüz kırk ila üç bin yedi yüz elli peso bandındadır. Bu, tercihli tarife uygulanan veya telafi edici vergiye tabi mallarda da böyledir. Ama tanım tutmuyorsa ya da yanlış kod bir izin, bir NOM veya telafi edici vergi yükümlülüğünü atlatıyorsa tablo tamamen değişir: mal el konulabilir ve para cezaları ticari değerin yüzde iki yüz elli ila üç yüzüne kadar çıkabilir. translations.title: Spanish Labeling For Amazon Mexico: What NOM Rules Require
translations.excerpt: Sellers often think the FNSKU label is enough. It is not. Mexico requires a separate Spanish label before the product can legally be sold, and Amazon will not apply it for you.
translations.content:
Yes, your Amazon Mexico products need a Spanish label, and it is a separate thing from the FNSKU barcode. The FNSKU is Amazon's internal identifier for fulfillment. The Spanish NOM label is a legal requirement for the product to enter Mexico and be sold there, and it must be applied before the goods are offered for sale, not after.

  • The FNSKU barcode and the Spanish NOM label serve different purposes and you need both.
  • NOM-050 sets general commercial labelling information for most non-food products (Secretaría de Economía).
  • NOM-051 applies to pre-packaged food and non-alcoholic beverages and carries the front-of-pack warning seals.
  • Sector standards apply on top: NOM-004 for textiles and clothing, NOM-141 for cosmetics.
  • The Spanish label must be in place before the product is offered for sale, so labelling at origin is almost always cheaper than relabelling in Mexico.

Do my Amazon Mexico products need Spanish labels?

Yes, and the label most sellers already have does not count. The FNSKU is Amazon's fulfillment barcode. The Spanish NOM label is a legal condition of importing and selling the product in Mexico. They are separate requirements and you need both.

The single most common and most expensive misunderstanding among sellers entering Amazon Mexico is thinking that the FNSKU label covers labelling. It does not, because the two labels answer to two different authorities. The FNSKU is Amazon's own identifier. It exists so the fulfillment centre can tell your unit apart from an identical unit belonging to another seller, and Amazon's rules govern how it looks and where it goes: black on white, scannable, removable, covering any conflicting manufacturer barcode. Nothing about it satisfies Mexican law. The Spanish NOM label is a completely separate thing. It exists because Mexican regulation requires that information reaching the consumer be in Spanish and contain specific data, and that requirement applies at the point the product enters the country and again at the point it is offered for sale. Customs can hold goods that arrive without it, and the obligation does not disappear because the product is sold through a marketplace. Amazon will not apply this label for you. Their prep services handle Amazon's own requirements, not another country's product regulation, so if your units arrive in Mexico carrying only an English label and an FNSKU sticker, you have a compliance problem regardless of how well the listing is doing. The practical consequence is that labelling has to be decided before the shipment moves, and for most sellers that means labelling at origin while the goods are still in a warehouse where labour and access are cheap.

Which NOM applies to your product?

NOM-050 covers general commercial information for most non-food products. NOM-051 covers pre-packaged food and non-alcoholic drinks, including the front-of-pack warning seals. Sector standards stack on top, such as NOM-004 for textiles and NOM-141 for cosmetics.

There is no single Mexican labelling rule, there is a base rule plus whatever applies to your category, and getting this pairing right is most of the work. For the majority of general retail goods the base standard is NOM-050, which sets out the commercial information a product must carry: what it is, who is responsible for it in Mexico with their tax identity, where it came from, and how to use and care for it. If your product is pre-packaged food or a non-alcoholic beverage, the governing standard is NOM-051 instead, and this is the one that brings the front-of-pack warning seals for excess calories, sugars, sodium, saturated fat and trans fat, along with the rules on when those seals block certain marketing elements. On top of the base, sector standards apply. Textiles and clothing fall under NOM-004, which requires fibre composition by percentage in descending order, care instructions, size, the responsible party with their Mexican tax identity, and country of origin, with the label physically sewn into garments rather than stuck on. Cosmetics fall under NOM-141. Supplements sit outside NOM-051 entirely and follow their own labelling appendix with two mandatory warning phrases. The pattern to remember is that you are never looking for one number. You are looking for the base standard for your product type plus any category standard, and both have to be satisfied on the same label.

What has to be on the label, and where do you apply it?

Product name, importer name and Mexican tax identity, country of origin, contents and use or care instructions, all in Spanish. Apply it at origin. Relabelling in Mexico is legal but costs per unit and delays the goods, and doing it after customs holds the shipment is the worst case.

Across the standards the recurring elements are consistent enough to plan around, even though the detail varies by category. You need the product name in Spanish, a full description of contents or composition, the name and address of the party responsible in Mexico together with their tax registration, the country of origin, and instructions for use, storage or care where the product needs them. Food adds the nutritional declaration and warning seals, textiles add fibre percentages and size, cosmetics add ingredient listing. The information must be legible, in Spanish, and present before the product is offered for sale. Note the phrase responsible party in Mexico, because it catches foreign sellers out. The label points at someone inside the country who answers for the product, and that is usually the importer of record. If you have no Mexican presence, this is one of the practical reasons sellers work with a partner who can act in that role. On placement, you have three options and they are not equal. Labelling at origin, while the goods sit in a US or overseas warehouse, is the cheapest and least disruptive, because you are applying labels to cartons that are already open and staffed. Labelling at a border facility before the goods cross is the middle option and works well when artwork was not ready in time. Relabelling inside Mexico after arrival is legal but the most expensive, because you are paying per unit under time pressure, and if the shipment was held at customs for missing labels you are also paying storage while you fix it. BringGo Ship applies Spanish NOM labelling in Laredo before the goods cross, which keeps the label question out of the customs queue.

Who applies itYou or your 3PLAmazon does not apply NOM labels

Definitions

  • FNSKU: The FNSKU is Amazon's own barcode that identifies your unit inside the fulfillment centre and has no regulatory meaning in Mexico.
  • NOM label: A NOM label is the Spanish language product label Mexican regulation requires before a product can enter and be sold.
  • Responsible party: The responsible party is the entity inside Mexico named on the label with its tax registration, usually the importer of record.

Frequently asked questions

Do Amazon Mexico products need a Spanish label?

Yes, and it is separate from the FNSKU barcode. The FNSKU is Amazon's fulfillment identifier and has no regulatory meaning. The Spanish NOM label is a legal condition of importing and selling the product in Mexico, and it must be in place before the product is offered for sale.

Will Amazon apply the Spanish label for me?

No. Amazon prep services handle Amazon's own requirements, such as barcoding and packaging, not another country's product regulation. If your units arrive carrying only an English label and an FNSKU sticker, you have a compliance problem even if the listing is live and selling.

Which NOM standard applies to my product?

Start with the base standard: NOM-050 for most general retail goods, NOM-051 for pre-packaged food and non-alcoholic beverages. Then add any category standard, such as NOM-004 for textiles or NOM-141 for cosmetics. You are never looking for one number, you are looking for base plus category.

Where should I apply the Spanish label?

At origin whenever possible. Labelling while goods are still in a warehouse abroad is the cheapest, because cartons are already open and staffed. Labelling at a border facility before crossing is a workable middle option. Relabelling inside Mexico after arrival costs the most per unit and is worse still if customs held the goods.

What does responsible party in Mexico mean on the label?

It means a party inside Mexico, named with its tax registration, that answers for the product. This is usually the importer of record. Foreign sellers with no Mexican presence often work with a partner who can take that role, because the label cannot simply point at an address abroad.

translations.title: Can You Ship Commercially To Mexico Without A Mexican Company?
translations.excerpt: You do not need a Mexican company to sell into Mexico. You do need someone registered in Mexico to act as importer of record, and which route you pick changes your tax exposure.
translations.content:
Yes, you can sell into Mexico without your own Mexican company, but a formal commercial import always needs an importer of record who is registered in Mexico and enrolled in the importer registry. Your options are to let the buyer import, to use a partner as importer of record, to ship small consignments under the simplified courier regime, or to set up your own entity.

  • A formal commercial import requires an importer of record registered in Mexico and enrolled in the Padrón de Importadores (SAT).
  • Only a licensed Mexican customs broker can file the pedimento that legalises the import (SAT).
  • The simplified courier regime is capped at 2,500 US dollars per consignee; above that a formal pedimento is required (RGCE 2026).
  • Amazon requires RFC tax information from sellers shipping from Mexico or with Mexican indicators (Amazon México).
  • Without an RFC on file, withholding runs at 16 percent IVA and 20 percent ISR, so verify your position with Seller Central and a tax adviser.

Can I ship commercially to Mexico without a Mexican company or RFC?

Yes, but not by importing in your own name. A commercial import needs an importer of record registered in Mexico. You can avoid setting up an entity by having the buyer import, using a partner as importer of record, or staying inside the simplified courier regime.

The question people are really asking is whether they need to incorporate in Mexico before they can start selling there, and the answer is no. What Mexico requires is not that you have a company, but that someone identifiable and registered inside the country takes legal responsibility for the import. That role is called the importer of record, and it carries the obligations: enrolment in the importer registry, tax identity, and liability for what was declared. A foreign company with no Mexican registration cannot fill that role itself. Alongside it, only a licensed Mexican customs broker can actually file the pedimento that legalises the entry, so the broker is never optional in a formal import either. Once you see it this way the routes become clear rather than mysterious. Either your buyer is the importer, or a partner is the importer, or the shipment is small enough to travel under the simplified courier regime where the recipient is treated as the importer, or you decide the volume justifies your own Mexican entity. Each of these is a legitimate way to sell into Mexico without a company of your own, and each one moves cost, control and risk to a different place. The mistake is not picking the wrong one, it is not picking deliberately and finding out at the border which one you defaulted into.

The four routes, and what each costs you

Buyer as importer is simplest but limits you to customers who can import. A partner as importer of record lets you sell to anyone and keeps control. The courier regime works under 2,500 dollars per consignee. Your own entity gives the most control and the most overhead.

Route one is letting your Mexican buyer act as importer of record. This is the least work for you and it is normal in B2B, because an established Mexican business is usually already enrolled in the importer registry. The limitation is obvious: you can only sell to buyers who can import, which rules out consumers and most small businesses, and you lose visibility over what happens after the border. Route two is using a partner as importer of record, typically a logistics operator or a specialised service. Here the partner imports on your behalf, the goods clear in their name, and you keep control of the inventory and the customer relationship. This is the route most cross-border sellers end up on because it lets you sell to anyone, including consumers, without incorporating. Route three is the simplified courier regime, which suits small parcels. It is capped at 2,500 US dollars per consignee and the recipient effectively bears the import, with a single combined rate applied instead of a full pedimento. It is genuinely useful for testing a market or for low value direct to consumer orders, but it is not a way to move commercial volume, and deliberately splitting a larger order into small parcels to stay under thresholds is a pattern the rules specifically watch for. Route four is your own Mexican entity with your own registry enrolment. This gives you the most control and is usually the right end state for a business with steady volume, but it brings accounting, tax filing and administration that only makes sense once the volume justifies it. Most sellers start on route one or three, move to route two as they grow, and only consider route four when Mexico becomes a core market.

The tax detail that decides the economics

If you sell on Amazon Mexico with Mexican indicators, Amazon requires RFC tax information. Without an RFC on file, withholding is substantially higher, which can remove the margin entirely. This is the single number that most often decides whether a route works.

There is one piece of arithmetic that changes the answer for marketplace sellers and it is worth being blunt about. Amazon requires RFC tax information from sellers shipping from Mexico or operating with Mexican indicators, and using FBA in Mexico means holding inventory in Mexico, which is exactly such an indicator. Where no RFC is on file, withholding applies at a much higher rate: the figures circulating for 2026 are 16 percent IVA and 20 percent ISR, against materially lower rates for a seller registered with an RFC and a Mexican bank account. If those numbers hold for your situation, more than a third of your gross revenue is withheld before it reaches you, and that is before the category referral fee and the fulfillment fee. In most categories that removes the margin completely. We flag this rather than state it as settled because the withholding rules were updated for 2026 and the precise rates should be confirmed in Seller Central and with a Mexican tax adviser before you build a plan around them. The direction and the scale, however, are not in doubt, and the practical conclusion follows: if your route to market is FBA in Mexico, the tax registration question is not an administrative detail you can defer, it is the first thing to resolve. For sellers who want to reach Mexican customers without taking that on immediately, importing through a partner and fulfilling from a Mexican warehouse keeps you selling while you decide. BringGo Ship operates warehouses in Laredo and Monterrey with a licensed customs broker in house, which is what makes the partner route practical rather than theoretical.

Four ways to sell into Mexico without your own entity

RouteWho importsBest for
Buyer importsYour Mexican customerB2B with established buyers
Partner as importer of recordYour logistics partnerSelling to anyone, keeping control
Simplified courier regimeThe recipientUnder 2,500 USD per consignee
Your own Mexican entityYouSteady volume, Mexico as core market
Always requiredLicensed customs brokerFiles the pedimento in every formal import

Definitions

  • Importer of record: The importer of record is the party registered in Mexico that takes legal responsibility for the import and what was declared.
  • Padrón de Importadores: The Padrón de Importadores is the Mexican importer registry an entity must be enrolled in to import commercially on a regular basis.
  • RFC: The RFC is the Mexican tax registration number, and its absence triggers substantially higher marketplace withholding.

Frequently asked questions

Can I ship commercially to Mexico without a Mexican company?

Yes. What Mexico requires is not that you have a company, but that someone registered in Mexico acts as importer of record. You can have the buyer import, use a partner as importer of record, stay inside the simplified courier regime, or set up your own entity. Only the last one requires incorporating.

Do I need a Mexican customs broker even without a company?

Yes, for any formal commercial import. Only a licensed Mexican customs broker can file the pedimento that legalises the entry, and that is independent of who the importer of record is. The broker is never the optional part. Small parcels under the simplified courier regime work differently and do not need a formal pedimento.

How large can a shipment be without a formal import?

The simplified courier regime is capped at 2,500 US dollars per consignee. Above that a formal pedimento is required, with a customs broker and an importer of record enrolled in the registry. Deliberately splitting a larger order into small parcels to stay under thresholds is a pattern the rules specifically watch for.

Do I need an RFC to sell on Amazon Mexico?

Amazon requires RFC tax information from sellers shipping from Mexico or with Mexican indicators, and holding FBA inventory in Mexico is such an indicator. Without an RFC on file, withholding is substantially higher, which in most categories removes the margin. Confirm your exact position in Seller Central and with a tax adviser.

Which route should I start with?

Most sellers start by having the buyer import or by using the courier regime for small orders, move to a partner acting as importer of record as volume grows, and only set up their own Mexican entity once Mexico is a core market. The mistake is not choosing, and finding out at the border which route you defaulted into.

translations.title: Importar Cosméticos A México: Lo Que COFEPRIS Realmente Pide
translations.excerpt: Los cosméticos no llevan registro sanitario, y por eso mucha gente supone que no están regulados. Sí lo están, solo que por otra vía. Esto es lo que COFEPRIS pide de verdad.
translations.content:
Los cosméticos no requieren registro sanitario en México, a diferencia de los medicamentos. Lo que sí requieren es que el establecimiento importador presente su aviso de funcionamiento, que el producto lleve etiqueta en español conforme a la NOM-141, que exista un responsable identificable dentro de México, y que los ingredientes cumplan las listas de sustancias permitidas y prohibidas.

  • Los cosméticos no están en la lista de productos que requieren registro sanitario (Ley General de Salud, art. 376).
  • El establecimiento importador debe presentar aviso de funcionamiento, que es una notificación y no una autorización previa.
  • El etiquetado de cosméticos se rige por la NOM-141 y debe estar en español antes de la comercialización.
  • Debe existir un responsable identificable dentro de México, con nombre y domicilio en la etiqueta.
  • Los ingredientes deben respetar las listas de sustancias permitidas y prohibidas que aplica COFEPRIS.

¿Qué pide COFEPRIS para importar cosméticos?

No pide registro sanitario del producto. Pide que el establecimiento importador tenga aviso de funcionamiento, que la etiqueta esté en español conforme a la NOM-141, que haya un responsable dentro de México y que los ingredientes cumplan las listas aplicables.

Conviene empezar por el malentendido más común, porque cuesta dinero en las dos direcciones. Es cierto que los cosméticos no requieren registro sanitario: la Ley General de Salud enumera qué productos necesitan ese trámite y los cosméticos no aparecen ahí. De esa verdad mucha gente salta a una conclusión falsa, que es suponer que los cosméticos entran sin más. La regulación existe, solo que opera por otra vía. Lo primero es el establecimiento, no el producto. El importador debe presentar su aviso de funcionamiento ante la autoridad sanitaria, que es una notificación con la que se declara la actividad, no una autorización que haya que esperar. Lo segundo es la etiqueta, que debe estar en español y cumplir la NOM-141, la norma específica de etiquetado cosmético, y debe estar puesta antes de que el producto se ofrezca al público. Lo tercero es que haya un responsable identificable dentro de México, con nombre y domicilio visibles en la etiqueta, porque una marca extranjera sin presencia local no puede quedar como único responsable frente al consumidor. Y lo cuarto son los ingredientes, que deben respetar las listas de sustancias permitidas y prohibidas. La diferencia práctica frente a un medicamento es real y grande, pero no equivale a ausencia de control: en cosméticos el control se ejerce sobre quién importa, qué dice la etiqueta y qué contiene el producto, no sobre un expediente de registro por cada referencia.

La etiqueta es donde se detienen los embarques

El motivo más frecuente de retención no es un permiso faltante, es una etiqueta en inglés o incompleta. La NOM-141 exige información en español antes de la comercialización, incluida la identificación del responsable en México y el listado de ingredientes.

Si tuvieras que elegir una sola cosa que revisar antes de embarcar, sería la etiqueta, porque es donde se detiene la mercancía con más frecuencia. La regla de fondo es simple de enunciar y fácil de incumplir: la información debe estar en español y debe estar antes de que el producto se comercialice, no después de que llegue. Para productos importados envasados en origen esto significa que la etiqueta en español tiene que viajar con el producto o aplicarse antes de ponerlo a la venta. La NOM-141 define qué debe aparecer, y los elementos que más se omiten son siempre los mismos: la identificación del responsable dentro de México con su domicilio, el listado de ingredientes, el contenido neto, el lote, y las advertencias o instrucciones de uso cuando el producto las necesita. Junto a esto hay un punto que atrapa a marcas extranjeras acostumbradas a otros mercados, y es el de las declaraciones. Un cosmético no puede presentarse con propiedades terapéuticas. Si la etiqueta o la publicidad atribuyen al producto la capacidad de tratar, prevenir o rehabilitar una condición, deja de ser cosmético a ojos de la autoridad y pasa a regirse por reglas mucho más estrictas. Frases que en otro país son marketing habitual pueden reclasificar tu producto aquí. Por eso la revisión de etiqueta debe hacerse sobre el texto en español real que va a ir pegado, no sobre una traducción aproximada del original.

Cómo lo organizas en la práctica

Define primero quién será el responsable en México, luego valida ingredientes contra las listas aplicables, después cierra el arte de etiqueta en español y etiqueta en origen. Dejar la etiqueta para el final es lo que convierte un trámite ordinario en mercancía detenida.

El orden importa más que la velocidad. Empieza por definir quién será el responsable dentro de México, porque de esa decisión dependen el aviso de funcionamiento y el nombre que irá en la etiqueta. Si tienes empresa en México, eres tú. Si no la tienes, esto se resuelve trabajando con un socio que pueda asumir ese papel, y conviene cerrarlo antes de comprar inventario, no después. El segundo paso es validar los ingredientes contra las listas de sustancias permitidas y prohibidas, sobre todo si tu producto incluye activos poco comunes o formulaciones pensadas para otro mercado, porque un ingrediente que allá es rutinario aquí puede estar restringido. El tercero es cerrar el arte de etiqueta en español con todos los datos obligatorios, y hacerlo revisar por alguien que conozca la norma antes de imprimir, ya que reimprimir es barato comparado con reetiquetar unidad por unidad. El cuarto es etiquetar en origen. Poner la etiqueta mientras la mercancía está todavía en una bodega, con personal disponible y sin reloj corriendo, siempre cuesta menos que hacerlo en México bajo presión, y evita que la etiqueta se convierta en el motivo de una demora aduanal. El quinto es documentar: factura, lista de empaque y descripción deben coincidir entre sí y con lo que realmente va en la caja. BringGo Ship opera bodegas en Laredo y Monterrey con agente aduanal con patente propio y aplica el etiquetado en español antes del cruce, precisamente para que la etiqueta no sea el cuello de botella.

Definiciones

  • Registro sanitario: El registro sanitario es la autorización por producto que exigen los medicamentos y ciertos dispositivos, y que los cosméticos no requieren.
  • Aviso de funcionamiento: El aviso de funcionamiento es la notificación con la que un establecimiento declara su actividad ante la autoridad sanitaria, sin esperar autorización.
  • NOM-141: La NOM-141 es la norma que define qué debe decir la etiqueta de un producto cosmético en México.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Los cosméticos necesitan registro sanitario en México?

No. La Ley General de Salud enumera qué productos requieren registro sanitario y los cosméticos no están en esa lista. Pero eso no significa que entren sin control: se exige aviso de funcionamiento del establecimiento importador, etiqueta en español conforme a la NOM-141, un responsable dentro de México y cumplimiento de ingredientes.

¿Qué es el aviso de funcionamiento y quién lo presenta?

Es una notificación con la que el establecimiento declara su actividad ante la autoridad sanitaria. Lo presenta el importador, no la marca extranjera, y es una notificación y no una autorización, así que no se espera una aprobación previa para operar. Aplica al establecimiento, no a cada producto.

¿Por qué se detienen los embarques de cosméticos?

El motivo más frecuente no es un permiso faltante, es la etiqueta. Llega en inglés, o le falta la identificación del responsable en México, el listado de ingredientes, el contenido neto o el lote. La norma exige que la información esté en español antes de comercializar, no después de que la mercancía llegue.

¿Puedo decir que mi cosmético trata una condición de la piel?

No. Si la etiqueta o la publicidad atribuyen al producto propiedades terapéuticas, preventivas o rehabilitadoras, deja de tratarse como cosmético y pasa a regirse por reglas mucho más estrictas. Frases que en otros mercados son marketing habitual pueden reclasificar el producto aquí, así que revisa el texto en español real.

¿Necesito empresa en México para importar cosméticos?

Necesitas un responsable identificable dentro de México, con nombre y domicilio en la etiqueta, y un establecimiento importador con aviso de funcionamiento. Si no tienes empresa propia, esto se resuelve con un socio que pueda asumir ese papel, y conviene cerrarlo antes de comprar inventario.

translations.title: Through-Trailer Vs Transload Vs Cross-Dock For Mexico Freight
translations.excerpt: The same shipment can cross the border three different ways, and the choice decides how many times your freight is handled. Here is how each model actually works.
translations.content:
Through-trailer means the same trailer crosses and only the tractor changes, so the freight is never touched. Transload means the goods move from a US trailer into a Mexican trailer at the border. Cross-dock means the goods are unloaded, re-sorted and rebuilt into new shipments before crossing. Fewer touches means less damage risk; more touches means more flexibility.

  • In all three models a drayage tractor handles the physical border crossing itself.
  • Through-trailer touches the freight zero times after loading, which is the lowest damage and shrinkage risk.
  • Transload moves goods between trailers once, which frees the US trailer to return quickly.
  • Cross-dock unloads and rebuilds shipments, which is what makes consolidation and multi-destination delivery possible.
  • A well documented truck reaches Monterrey from Laredo in one to two business days in all three models (operational data).

Through-trailer, transload or cross-dock: which is best for my freight?

Through-trailer if you have a full trailer going to one destination and want the freight untouched. Transload if you want your US equipment back quickly. Cross-dock if you are combining suppliers or splitting to several destinations.

All three describe what happens to your goods at the border, and the difference between them is simply how many times someone handles the freight. Through-trailer is the model with zero handling. Your loaded trailer arrives at the border, a drayage tractor picks it up and pulls it across the bridge, and a Mexican carrier takes it onward to the destination. The goods themselves never move; only the tractor pulling them changes. Transload is the model with one handling. Your goods arrive in a US trailer, they are moved across a dock into a Mexican trailer, and that trailer continues to the destination. Your US equipment turns around and goes back into service instead of sitting in Mexico. Cross-dock is the model with restructuring. Goods come off the inbound trailer, get sorted on the dock, and go back out in a different configuration entirely: several suppliers combined into one shipment, or one shipment split into several deliveries. Nothing is stored, everything moves through, which is what separates cross-dock from warehousing. The reason this matters commercially is that each handling is both a cost and a risk. Every time a pallet is moved there is a chance of damage, a chance of a miscount, and a labour charge. So the honest rule is to use the fewest touches your operation actually needs, and no fewer. Choosing through-trailer when you genuinely need to consolidate four suppliers will not save you anything, it will just move the problem somewhere more expensive.

What each model actually costs you

Through-trailer has the lowest handling cost but ties up your trailer and requires a full load to one destination. Transload adds one handling charge and frees your equipment. Cross-dock costs the most in handling but is the only model that lowers your customs cost per unit.

The cost comparison only makes sense if you look past the handling fee, because the handling fee is rarely the biggest number. Through-trailer has the lowest direct handling cost, since nobody unloads anything, but it carries a hidden one: your trailer goes to Mexico and stays there until it comes back, which is equipment out of service. For a company running its own fleet that matters; for a company buying capacity by the load it usually does not. Transload adds a single handling charge and buys back that equipment time, which is why it is common among US shippers who want their trailers turning. It also lets you switch to Mexican equipment sized for the destination, which can matter for urban delivery. Cross-dock has the highest handling cost per shipment and is still frequently the cheapest overall, and the reason is customs rather than trucking. The fixed costs of an import, meaning the broker fee, the prevalidation and the processing fee, are paid per pedimento rather than per pallet. Combining four suppliers into one import spreads those fixed costs across four times the goods. If you are importing small volumes from several sources, that arithmetic usually beats the handling charge by a wide margin. The other thing cross-dock buys is flexibility on the far side: because shipments are rebuilt anyway, you can send different pallets to different Mexican destinations from the same crossing, instead of paying for domestic redistribution afterwards.

Picking the right one

Ask three questions: is it a full load, does it go to one destination, and are you combining suppliers? Full load to one place means through-trailer. Full load but you want your trailer back means transload. Anything involving multiple suppliers or destinations means cross-dock.

In practice the decision comes down to three questions and you can answer them before you ask anyone for a quote. First, is this a full trailer or a partial load? If it is partial, you are going to be consolidated with someone else's freight regardless, so cross-dock is where you already are. Second, does everything go to one destination? If yes, handling the goods adds risk without adding value, and through-trailer or transload is right. If several destinations, cross-dock lets you build the delivery legs once instead of paying twice. Third, are you combining goods from more than one supplier? If yes, cross-dock is the only model that lets you do it before the import, which is where the customs saving lives. A common pattern for growing sellers looks like this: they start with courier parcels, move to cross-dock consolidation as soon as they have more than one supplier, and only graduate to through-trailer when a single destination pulls full trailer volumes. Going backwards down that path is rare. Whichever model you use, the transit itself is not the variable people expect. A well documented truck reaches Monterrey from Laredo in one to two business days in all three cases, because the distance is a few hours of driving plus customs. What changes the timeline is documentation quality, not the crossing model. BringGo Ship runs warehouses on both sides of the border in Laredo and Monterrey with a licensed customs broker in house, so consolidation, clearance and the onward leg sit in one chain rather than three.

Three ways freight crosses into Mexico

ModelTimes freight is handledBest when
Through-trailerZero, tractor changes onlyFull load, one destination
TransloadOnce, trailer to trailerYou want US equipment back
Cross-dockUnloaded and rebuiltMultiple suppliers or destinations
Customs cost per unitSameCross-dock lowers it by consolidating
Damage and miscount riskLowest on through-trailerRises with each handling
Laredo to Monterrey transit1 to 2 business daysSame in all three if documents are clean

Definitions

  • Through-trailer: Through-trailer means the same loaded trailer crosses the border and only the tractor pulling it changes.
  • Transload: Transload means moving goods from one trailer to another at the border so each side keeps its own equipment.
  • Cross-dock: Cross-dock means unloading, re-sorting and rebuilding shipments at the border without putting anything into storage.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between transload and cross-dock?

Transload moves the same shipment from one trailer to another without changing what is in it. Cross-dock unloads goods and rebuilds them into different shipments, combining several suppliers or splitting to several destinations. Transload changes the equipment, cross-dock changes the shipment.

Which crossing model is cheapest?

Through-trailer has the lowest handling cost, but cross-dock is often cheapest overall when you import from several suppliers. Customs fixed costs like the broker fee and processing charges are paid per pedimento, not per pallet, so consolidating spreads them across more goods and usually beats the extra handling charge.

Does cross-docking slow down my shipment?

Not meaningfully. A well documented truck reaches Monterrey from Laredo in one to two business days in all three models, because the distance is a few hours of driving plus customs. What changes the timeline is documentation quality, not whether the freight was re-sorted at the border.

Is my freight at more risk if it gets handled?

Yes, in the sense that every handling adds a chance of damage or a miscount. That is the honest argument for through-trailer when you have a full load to a single destination. But avoiding handling you actually need does not remove the cost, it moves it, usually into domestic redistribution on the Mexican side.

Which model should a growing seller start with?

Most start with courier parcels, then move to cross-dock consolidation as soon as they buy from more than one supplier, because that is where the customs saving appears. Through-trailer becomes relevant later, when a single destination pulls full trailer volumes on its own.

translations.title: Warehousing In Nuevo Leon: Why The Monterrey Metro Works For Fulfillment
translations.excerpt: Most cross-border sellers end up holding stock in the Monterrey metro area, and it is not an accident. The geography does something no other location in Mexico does.
translations.content:
Nuevo Leon works for fulfillment because it is the first major industrial and consumer market inside Mexico after the busiest land border crossing. A well documented truck reaches Monterrey from Laredo in one to two business days, which means you can restock quickly from the US side while still shipping to Mexican customers as a domestic parcel.

  • Laredo is the busiest land port in North America, and Nuevo Leon is the first major market inland from it (WorldCity, Census).
  • A well documented truck reaches Monterrey from Laredo in one to two business days (operational data).
  • From a Monterrey warehouse, delivery to Mexican customers is a domestic parcel rather than an import.
  • Trucking carries roughly 73 to 74 percent of US Mexico trade, so the corridor is served by deep carrier capacity (WorldCity, Census).
  • Nuevo Leon has been one of the main destinations of nearshoring investment in Mexico, which is why industrial space concentrates there.

Why locate fulfillment in the Monterrey metro area?

Because it is close enough to the border to restock in a day or two, and deep enough inside Mexico that shipping to customers is domestic. Most other locations give you one of those two things, not both.

If you look at where cross-border sellers actually keep their Mexican inventory, the Monterrey metropolitan area comes up again and again, and the reason is a specific piece of geography rather than a preference. Nuevo Leon sits a few hours of driving inland from Laredo, which is the busiest land port in North America and the crossing that handles the bulk of US Mexico trade. That proximity means a well documented truck moves from a Laredo warehouse to a Monterrey warehouse in one to two business days. At the same time, Monterrey is a genuine internal market and a national distribution point, so a parcel leaving a warehouse there reaches a Mexican customer as an ordinary domestic shipment rather than an international one. Most alternatives give you one of these and not the other. A warehouse further south, closer to Mexico City, puts you nearer the largest population concentration but makes restocking from the US a longer and more expensive leg, which forces you to hold more inventory as a buffer. A warehouse only on the US side keeps restocking trivial but leaves every customer order crossing the border individually, with the cost and delay that implies. Nuevo Leon is the point where both work at once: short replenishment from the north, domestic delivery to the south. That is why the model most sellers converge on is a pair of warehouses, one in Laredo for consolidation and one in the Monterrey metro for fulfillment, rather than a single site anywhere.

What the industrial corridor gives you

Depth of supply. Nuevo Leon has absorbed a large share of nearshoring investment, so there is real industrial space, established carriers and available labour. Santa Catarina and the surrounding municipalities are part of that corridor.

Geography explains why the location works, but availability explains why it is practical, and this is where Nuevo Leon separates from places that look similar on a map. The state has been one of the main destinations of nearshoring investment in Mexico, and that investment has produced the things a fulfillment operation actually needs: purpose built industrial space rather than converted buildings, carriers that already run the routes daily, customs brokers with volume on the corridor, and a labour market used to warehouse and manufacturing work. The industrial footprint spreads across the Monterrey metropolitan area rather than sitting in one place, and municipalities such as Santa Catarina, Apodaca and Escobedo host a large share of it. For a foreign seller the practical consequence is choice: you are not negotiating with the only operator who can take your pallets, and you are not waiting weeks for a carrier slot. Depth of supply also matters for the thing nobody plans for, which is peak. Mexican retail concentrates heavily around Hot Sale in the spring and Buen Fin in November, and those weeks are exactly when a thin market fails you. Being in a corridor with real capacity means you can add temporary space or extra pickups when volume spikes rather than discovering that the one carrier serving your area is full. That is worth more than a slightly cheaper square metre rate in a quieter location, and it is a large part of why fulfillment concentrates where it does.

How the two-warehouse model works in practice

Consolidate in Laredo, import in one shipment, hold sellable stock in the Monterrey metro, ship domestically to customers, and return to the same Mexican address. Replenish on a reorder point rather than by guessing.

The operational shape most sellers land on is simple enough to describe in a paragraph, and it is worth setting up deliberately rather than arriving at by accident. Goods from your suppliers arrive at a Laredo warehouse, where they are received, consolidated and prepared, which means Spanish NOM labelling and anything else the product needs before it can be sold in Mexico. When there is enough volume to justify it, the consolidated load is imported in a single shipment rather than many small ones, which spreads the fixed customs costs across more goods. The load crosses and arrives at the Monterrey area warehouse in one to two business days. From there, customer orders ship domestically, at domestic prices and domestic speeds, and returns come back to the same Mexican address instead of crossing the border one parcel at a time. Replenishment runs on a reorder point per product rather than on someone remembering, so when stock in Mexico drops below a set level the next consolidation is triggered automatically. Because the northern leg is short, the stock you hold in Mexico can be small, which is the part that surprises people: proximity to the border is what lets you run lean rather than what forces you to hold more. The alternative, holding months of inventory because replenishment is slow, ties up capital in exactly the products that may not sell. BringGo Ship operates this model directly, with warehouses in Laredo and Monterrey and a licensed Mexican customs broker in house, so consolidation, clearance, fulfillment and returns sit in one chain.

Where to hold Mexican inventory

Definitions

  • Two-warehouse model: The two-warehouse model pairs a consolidation warehouse on the US side with a fulfillment warehouse inside Mexico.
  • Reorder point: A reorder point is the stock level that automatically triggers the next replenishment shipment.
  • Monterrey metro: The Monterrey metropolitan area is the industrial corridor in Nuevo Leon that includes municipalities such as Santa Catarina, Apodaca and Escobedo.

Frequently asked questions

Why locate fulfillment in the Monterrey metro area?

Because it is close enough to Laredo to restock in one to two business days and deep enough inside Mexico that shipping to customers is a domestic parcel. Most other locations give you one of those two things but not both, which is why cross-border sellers concentrate there.

Why not just hold everything in a US warehouse?

Because then every customer order crosses the border individually, carrying its own formalities, cost and delay. Restocking stays easy but the customer experience and the per-order cost both suffer. Holding sellable stock inside Mexico turns each order into an ordinary domestic delivery.

Why not a warehouse in central Mexico instead?

Central Mexico puts you closer to the largest population concentration, but replenishment from the US becomes a longer and more expensive leg. That forces you to hold more buffer inventory, which ties up capital. Nuevo Leon keeps replenishment short while still delivering domestically.

How much inventory do I need to hold in Mexico?

Less than most people expect, because the northern leg is short. You are covering the replenishment window rather than stockpiling, so a few weeks of sales of your fastest moving products is often enough. Proximity to the border is what lets you run lean rather than what forces you to hold more.

Does peak season change the calculation?

Yes, and it argues for the corridor rather than against it. Mexican retail concentrates around Hot Sale in the spring and Buen Fin in November, and those are the weeks a thin local market fails you. A corridor with real carrier and space capacity lets you add pickups or temporary space instead of being told everything is full.

translations.title: De Laredo A Full: La Ruta Logística Para Abastecer Mercado Libre
translations.excerpt: Mercado Libre Full no puede recibir tu importación directamente. Entre tu proveedor y el centro de Full siempre hay un paso más, y ahí es donde se gana o se pierde el margen.
translations.content:
No se puede enviar mercancía del extranjero directamente a Full. La mercancía tiene que importarse a México primero, con un importador registrado y un pedimento, y solo entonces puede entregarse al centro de Full como envío nacional. La ruta práctica es consolidar en Laredo, preparar y etiquetar ahí, importar en un solo embarque y entregar a Full desde una bodega mexicana.

  • Full recibe mercancía nacional ya nacionalizada, no importaciones directas desde el extranjero.
  • La importación requiere un importador registrado en el padrón y un pedimento presentado por agente aduanal con patente (SAT).
  • La etiqueta en español conforme a la NOM aplicable debe estar puesta antes de que el producto se comercialice.
  • Consolidar varios proveedores en una sola importación reparte los costos fijos del pedimento entre más unidades.
  • Un camión bien documentado llega de Laredo a Monterrey en uno o dos días hábiles (dato operativo).

¿Cómo llevo producto de EE.UU. directo a Full?

Directo no se puede. Full recibe mercancía que ya está nacionalizada, así que primero hay una importación con importador registrado y pedimento. Lo que sí puedes hacer es que ese paso ocurra una sola vez, en la frontera, y que la entrega a Full salga ya como envío nacional.

Conviene empezar por lo que no funciona, porque es el error que más tiempo cuesta. Full es un centro de fulfillment nacional: recibe inventario que ya está legalmente en México. No es una aduana ni un importador, así que no puede recibir un embarque que viene del extranjero sin nacionalizar. Cuando alguien pregunta cómo enviar directo de Estados Unidos a Full, la respuesta honesta es que ese envío directo no existe, y quien lo promete está omitiendo un paso que igual va a ocurrir, solo que sin que tú lo controles. La ruta real tiene tres tramos. Primero, la mercancía se junta en una bodega del lado estadounidense, normalmente en Laredo, donde se recibe de uno o varios proveedores. Segundo, ahí mismo se prepara: se revisa, se etiqueta en español conforme a la norma que aplique al producto, y se arma el expediente documental para la importación. Tercero, se importa en un solo embarque, con un importador registrado en el padrón y un pedimento presentado por un agente aduanal con patente, y una vez del lado mexicano la mercancía viaja a Full como cualquier envío nacional. Visto así, la pregunta correcta deja de ser cómo saltarse la importación y pasa a ser cómo hacerla una sola vez y bien, porque cada importación separada vuelve a cobrar los mismos costos fijos.

Dónde se gana el margen

En consolidar. Los costos fijos de una importación se pagan por pedimento, no por caja, así que juntar varios proveedores en un solo embarque baja el costo por unidad. Etiquetar en origen es la segunda palanca, porque reetiquetar en México se cobra por pieza.

Si comparas dos vendedores con el mismo producto y el mismo precio de compra, la diferencia de margen casi siempre está en dos decisiones tomadas antes de cruzar. La primera es consolidar. Los costos fijos de una importación, que son el honorario del agente aduanal, la prevalidación y el derecho de trámite, se pagan por pedimento sin importar cuánta mercancía traigas. Traer poco y seguido significa pagar esos montos completos una y otra vez. Juntar varios proveedores o varias semanas de compra en un solo embarque reparte el mismo costo entre muchas más unidades, y esa es la palanca más grande que tiene un vendedor que apenas empieza. La segunda es etiquetar en origen. Tu producto necesita etiqueta en español conforme a la norma aplicable antes de comercializarse, y ponerla mientras la mercancía está en una bodega, con personal y sin prisa, cuesta una fracción de lo que cuesta reetiquetar pieza por pieza en México. Si además la mercancía se detiene por etiqueta faltante, al costo de reetiquetado se le suma el almacenaje mientras se resuelve. Hay una tercera decisión menos visible pero igual de cara: el IVA de importación del 16 por ciento se paga al entrar la mercancía. Es acreditable, pero mientras tanto es efectivo inmovilizado, y si importas de más antes de saber qué rota, ese dinero queda atrapado en inventario que no se mueve. Por eso conviene que la primera importación sea deliberadamente conservadora.

Cómo se arma la operación

Define quién importa, consolida en Laredo, etiqueta ahí, importa en un embarque, entrega a Full desde bodega mexicana y repón por punto de reorden. Mantén stock propio fuera de Full para los productos que no rotan.

La secuencia práctica es corta y conviene fijarla antes de comprar inventario. Primero, define quién será el importador. Si tienes empresa en México con padrón, eres tú. Si no la tienes, se resuelve con un socio que pueda importar por ti, y eso hay que cerrarlo antes de que la mercancía se mueva, no cuando ya está en la frontera. Segundo, consolida en Laredo: que tus proveedores envíen ahí y que la bodega reciba, cuente y revise. Tercero, prepara en esa misma bodega: etiqueta en español, empaque adecuado y cualquier requisito específico de tu categoría. Cuarto, importa en un solo embarque y cruza; un camión bien documentado llega a Monterrey en uno o dos días hábiles. Quinto, entrega a Full desde la bodega mexicana como envío nacional, con las cantidades que realmente vas a vender en las próximas semanas. Y aquí va el consejo que más dinero ahorra: no mandes todo a Full. Full cobra por almacenar, así que conviene enviar ahí solo los productos con rotación y mantener el resto en tu propia bodega, reponiendo Full conforme se vende. Un punto de reorden por producto automatiza esa decisión y evita que alguien tenga que acordarse.
